profile.summary: GENERator is a family of generative DNA language models: it reads a DNA sequence and predicts what comes next, so it can both generate new sequence and produce embeddings for downstream tasks. The models are Transformer decoders that read DNA in 6-letter chunks (6-mers), with a context of up to 98k base pairs. The first release was trained on 386 billion nucleotides of eukaryotic DNA; a second release (GENERator-v2) adds eukaryote and prokaryote models.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: Overview and Important Notice; arXiv abstract; model card: Example 2

summary_quotes.text: we present GENERator, a collection of generative genomic foundation models utilizing the transformer decoder architecture
with a context length of 98k nucleotides, pre-trained on 386 billion nucleotides of eukaryotic DNA

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GENERator is a decoder-only Transformer trained as a causal language model on DNA: it predicts the next token from the tokens before it. DNA is split into 6-mer tokens. The first-release 1.2B checkpoint uses a Llama-type configuration with 26 layers, hidden size 2048, 32 attention heads and 4 key-value heads, a vocabulary of 4128 tokens and up to 16384 token positions. Embeddings are read from the last hidden layer, either at the last token or averaged over all tokens. GENERator-v2 adds a training objective that recovers single-nucleotide likelihoods from k-mer tokens, and pretraining data concentrated on gene-centric and regulatory regions.

sections.body: Six base checkpoints are listed. The first release has a 1.2B and a 3B eukaryote model trained on 386B of data. GENERator-v2 has 1.2B and 3B eukaryote models (422B of data) and 1.2B and 3B prokaryote models (515B of data). A 2026-07-06 notice asks users to re-download GENERator-prokaryote-1.2b-base and GENERator-prokaryote-3b-base, linking to the v2 prokaryote weights, so a result must name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer decoder with a 6-mer tokenizer. First-release 1.2B checkpoint: Llama-type configuration (GENERatorForCausalLM), 26 layers, hidden size 2048, 32 attention heads, 4 key-value heads, intermediate size 5632.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequence as text. For generation, the input length must be a multiple of 6, by left padding with A or left truncation; the card's examples prepend a <s> token.
facts.source_locator: README.md: Important Notice; model card: Example 1

quotes.text: please ensure that the length of each input sequence is a multiple of **6**
processed_sequences = ["<s>" + seq[len(seq)%6:] for seq in sequences]

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Generated DNA continuations, or embeddings taken from the last hidden layer (last-token or mean-pooled). The repository scripts also run zero-shot variant effect prediction and fine-tuned classification or regression.

strengths.text: Long context for a DNA language model: 98k base pairs per input.

quotes.text: a generative genomic foundation model for long-context DNA modeling, with a context length of 98k nucleotides

strengths.text: One model serves both generation and representation: the card shows sequence generation and embedding extraction, and the repository has scripts for variant effect prediction, fine-tuning on classification and regression, and causal language model fine-tuning.
strengths.source_locator: model card: How to use; README.md: Downstream

strengths.text: The authors report zero-shot variant effect prediction competitive with alignment-based methods without needing an alignment.

quotes.text: In a zero-shot setting, GENERator achieves competitive variant effect prediction performance relative to alignment-based methods, while remaining fully alignment-free and broadly applicable across species.

strengths.text: The GENERator-eukaryote-1.2b-base weights are MIT licensed and not gated; the other checkpoints were not checked.
strengths.source_locator: Hugging Face API response, cardData.license and gated

limitations.text: Generation input must be a multiple of 6 bases long; otherwise the tokenizer appends an out-of-vocabulary token and generation can degrade into repeated AAAAAA.

quotes.text: If the input sequence length is not a multiple of **6**, the tokenizer will append an `'<oov>'` (out-of-vocabulary) token to the end of the token sequence. This can result in uninformative subsequent generations, such as repeated `'AAAAAA'`.

limitations.text: The published examples load the model on a CUDA GPU with FlashAttention 2 and custom model code (trust_remote_code); running without these is not described.

The README's 2026-07-06 notice asks users to re-download GENERator-prokaryote-1.2b-base and GENERator-prokaryote-3b-base, linking to the v2 prokaryote repository, so prokaryote results from before and after that date may come from different weights.

quotes.text: please re-download the [weights](https://huggingface.co/GenerTeam/GENERator-v2-prokaryote-1.2b-base) for optimal performance

limitations.text: At 1.2B and 3B parameters the models are large; the sources read do not state the memory or hardware needed for inference.

run_guide.summary: Clone the repository, install its requirements, load the first-release 1.2B eukaryote checkpoint and generate a short continuation of two DNA sequences.
prerequisites: A CUDA GPU: the model card's example moves the model and inputs to cuda and uses FlashAttention 2. Memory needs are not stated.
Network access to huggingface.co, or the hf-mirror.com endpoint the README suggests.
Weights are MIT licensed per the model card.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/GenerTeam/GENERator.git
cd GENERator
git checkout --detach 5132e2c35da5d5e9a7dcec7484901be4de864bf6
steps.explanation: The README's clone commands. The checkout line is added by Rewire to pin the commit that was read.

steps.title: Install requirements
steps.shell:
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation
steps.explanation: The README installs requirements with Python 3.10. It recommends FlashAttention for long pretraining; it is included here because the card's example loads the model with flash_attention_2.

steps.title: Load the model and generate
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "GenerTeam/GENERator-eukaryote-1.2b-base",
    attn_implementation="flash_attention_2",
    trust_remote_code=True,
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
).cuda().eval()

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    "GenerTeam/GENERator-eukaryote-1.2b-base",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)

sequences = [
    "ATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCG",
    "ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGT"
]

processed_sequences = ["<s>" + seq[len(seq)%6:] for seq in sequences]

inputs = tokenizer(
    processed_sequences,
    add_special_tokens=False,
    return_tensors="pt",
    padding=True,
    padding_side="left",
).to("cuda")

with torch.inference_mode():
    outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=32, do_sample=False)

decoded_sequences = tokenizer.batch_decode(outputs, skip_special_tokens=True)
print(decoded_sequences)
PY
steps.explanation: Example 1 from the model card, wrapped in a shell heredoc with its comments removed. It downloads the weights from Hugging Face.

notes: The only existing source is the GENEB leaderboard, a benchmark that evaluated the model. The record description covers the first release (98 kb, 386 billion nucleotides) and both kingdoms; the v2 models are part of the same family. The GenerTeam Hugging Face organisation also has GENERanno models (annotation models), which are a different family and not covered. The bioRxiv page of the v2 preprint returned 429 at first and 200 on the retry; the abstract had already been saved from Europe PMC, which is the copy used.
